scope: Data files and one tag script copied verbatim into the server profile; no mod JAR and no Society file is changed

unbreakable_blocks.reason: already immovable for the physics assembler: SimAssemblyContraption.movementAllowed refuses a block whose destroy speed is -1, and Society registers all seven with hardness -1

preconditions.note: the array applied with unbreakableTags, lines 809-830
createSkullVariant ends with .unbreakable() (KubeJS BlockBuilder: hardness -1) for the six society:skull_* blocks; society:cavern_air has .hardness(-1)

storage_blocks_in_society_data_tags.reason: outside the two lists of handleItemBlockFluidTags.js that the script mirrors, so the physics assembler still moves them. A physics move does not duplicate their contents: the Sophisticated Storage block entity is Clearable, so moveBlocks empties it after saving its NBT, and the Functional Storage drawer blocks drop nothing in onRemove. The four controller blocks of the drawer tag do drop their upgrade slots; they are covered by sable:silent_assembly_removal instead. Adding the storage blocks to simulated:non_movable would only decide whether such storage may be part of a physics contraption.

preconditions.note: create:non_movable gets the six Sophisticated Storage chests and #functionalstorage:drawer
c:relocation_not_supported gets #functionalstorage:drawer
block tag functionalstorage:drawer, 142 ids
implements Clearable; clearContent empties the inventory and the upgrade handler

getDynamicDrops returns an empty list, so Titanium BasicBlock.onRemove drops nothing; the same override is in CompactingDrawerBlock, SimpleCompactingDrawerBlock, EnderDrawerBlock, FluidDrawerBlock and ArmoryCabinetBlock

files.purpose: Adds pixelmon:pixelmon, pixelmon:statue and pixelmon:bike to moblassos:diamond_lasso_blacklist so the diamond lasso cannot store them in an item. All three extend AbstractHorse (an Animal, not an Enemy), which is exactly what LassoItem$Type.DIAMOND accepts; canPlayerPickUp rejects entity types in this tag. The diamond lasso is sold by Society (kubejs/data/society_trading/shops/shepherd.json, trade shepherd_mob_lasso_for_sun); config/moblassos-server.toml diamond_lasso_time = -1.

preconditions.note: also absent from the official server pack ZIP
values is empty; the tag id and folder are the ones Mob Lassos registers (ModRegistry.registerEntityTypeTag("diamond_lasso_blacklist"), namespace moblassos)
canPlayerPickUp: !entityType.is(blacklist) && mobFilter
registers entity types pixelmon:pixelmon, pixelmon:statue, pixelmon:bike
only the Mob Lassos JAR defines moblassos:*_lasso_blacklist; kubejs/data has no moblassos folder

files.purpose: Template pool pixelmon:npc/gyms/fairy, missing from Pixelmon 9.2.3. The Fairy gym building has 8 jigsaws that draw from it, so without the pool the gym generates with no leader and no trainers. The file is Pixelmon's npc/gyms/grass.json with every "grass" replaced by "fairy": 21 single_pool_element entries, weight 1, processors minecraft:empty, projection rigid, fallback minecraft:empty.

files.purpose: Adds 74 blocks to sable:silent_assembly_removal. 23 are blocks that Society marks immovable: the 18 KubeJS blocks whose block entity has an inventory attachment, society_trading:auto_trader (a Java block of the Society Trading mod with four item slots) and the four Functional Storage controller blocks of Society's block tag functionalstorage:drawer (storage controller and controller extension, plain and framed; their block entity holds upgrade items). SubLevelAssemblyHelper.moveBlocks copies each block entity as NBT to the new position; for a block in this tag it removes the old block entity first, so when the old block is later replaced by air the block's onRemove finds no block entity and drops nothing (KubeJS BasicBlockJS.onRemove -> InventoryAttachment.onRemove = Containers.dropContents; AutoTraderBlock.onRemove -> AutoTraderBlockEntity.drops; Titanium BasicBlock.onRemove -> Containers.dropContents of getDynamicDrops, which the two controller block classes do not override). Without the tag the items stay in the old block entity too (none of BlockEntityJS, AutoTraderBlockEntity and ControllableDrawerTile is Clearable) and are dropped as well. moveBlocks is the only block mover of the port: assembly (SimAssemblyHelper.assembleFromSingleBlock -> assembleBlocks), disassembly (SimAssemblyHelper.disassembleSubLevel, also used by merging glue), sub-level split (SubLevelHeatMapManager -> assembleBlocks) and Sable's assemble command (SableAssembleCommands) all go through it. The other 51 ids are Pixelmon blocks with the same defect (added by the second review): the 48 gym signs (GymSignBlock.onRemove drops the item shown in the sign when GymSignTileEntity.itemDrops is true, the default), pixelmon:fossil_display (FossilDisplayBlock.onRemove spawns the displayed fossil item), pixelmon:cloning_machine (CloningMachineBlock.onRemove spawns a cloning_machine item, or an aluminium ingot when broken, and calls CloningMachineTileEntity.onDestroy, which puts the stored Mew back into the owner's party) and pixelmon:infuser (InfuserBlock.onRemove drops getInfuserItemStacks(); InfuserTileEntity is a WorldlyContainer, but its clearContent is an empty method, so Sable's Clearable.tryClear leaves the items in place). The gym sign, fossil display and cloning machine block entities are not Clearable. Each of the four saves that state in its NBT (ItemIn / ItemIn / Mew / Items), so without the tag a physics move leaves the item or the Mew at the old position and in the moved block. Pixelmon's remaining onRemove droppers (box, end table, fridge, mower) extend InventoryTileEntity, whose clearContent (IBasicInventory default) empties every slot; Sable clears them before the old block is removed, so they are left out. These ten are all the onRemove overrides in the Pixelmon JAR. Not covered by this file: block entities of other mods that drop in onRemove and are not Clearable (see physics_assembly_duplication_not_covered).

files.purpose: Server script: ServerEvents.tags("block") handler adding Society's 52 immovable blocks (33 listed with immovableTags plus the 19 global.artisanMachineIds) to simulated:non_movable, the only tag the port's physics assembler (SimAssemblyContraption.movementAllowed) consults. The ids are listed in the script and global.artisanMachineIds is additionally read when the handler runs; both sources are unioned. The listed ids are added before the global is read, so a missing or unreadable global cannot drop them. Nothing is read from or removed from any tag, so handler order does not matter. The wider tags create:non_movable / c:relocation_not_supported are not forwarded.

physics_assembly_duplication_not_covered.scope: sable:silent_assembly_removal in this overlay lists Society's inventory blocks, the four Functional Storage controllers and the Pixelmon blocks above. Sable's moveBlocks duplicates the contents of every other block whose block entity is not Clearable and whose Block.onRemove drops them; the port ships its own list of 17 third-party ids for the same reason.

proven_from_bytes_not_fixed_here.evidence: ItemVaultBlock.onRemove: level.getBlockEntity(pos) instanceof ItemVaultBlockEntity -> ItemHelper.dropContents(vaultBE.inventory); ItemVaultBlockEntity extends SmartBlockEntity and is not Clearable; no class of create-1.20.1-6.0.8.jar implements net.minecraft.world.Clearable (only CloneCommand references it); the port has no mixin on a Create onRemove or destroy path. Create's own Contraption.removeBlocksFromWorld calls level.removeBlockEntity before setting air, which is what the silent tag makes Sable do.

physics_assembly_duplication_not_covered.leads_not_verified: Create blocks that end in IBE.onRemove -> SmartBlockEntity.destroy() or drop in their own onRemove were not read one by one. A pack-wide byte scan by the first review lists 57 block classes whose onRemove references a drop call next to a block entity that is not a Container or Clearable, 14 of them in create-1.20.1-6.0.8.jar (CopycatBlock, PlacardBlock, ItemDrainBlock, FluidPipeBlock, BeltBlock, MechanicalCrafterBlock, CrushingWheelControllerBlock, AbstractChuteBlock, FactoryPanelBlock, ItemVaultBlock, BasinBlock, LecternControllerBlock, SchematicannonBlock, SchematicTableBlock): <scratch>/fixes/overlay-data-review/onremove_triage.json. The scan is heuristic in both directions: it lists Pixelmon MysteryBoxBlock, which drops nothing in onRemove, and it clears every Container block entity, although a Container with an empty clearContent (Pixelmon InfuserTileEntity) still duplicates.
physics_assembly_duplication_not_covered.runtime_probe: setblock create:item_vault, insert 6 minecraft:diamond through a hopper, "sable assemble area" over the vault: count minecraft:diamond item entities at the old position (0 = no duplication) and read the Inventory of the moved block entity.

later_changes: After this note was written, sable:silent_assembly_removal was extended from 74 to 310 ids: every block the in-game sweep (tests/forge-assembly-probe.js, evidence/assembly-inventory-sweep-baseline.json) saw duplicating its contents was added. The sweep confirmed the 48 Pixelmon gym signs and the Society blocks at run time; pixelmon:cloning_machine, fossil_display and infuser stay on the bytecode proof alone, because Pixelmon's multi-block machines cannot be placed next to the port's physics (evidence/pixelmon-multiblock-physics-crash.json).
The current tag hash and preconditions are in compat/coexistence-build.json and compat/coexistence/preconditions.json; hashes of that file quoted in this note are the earlier ones.
